title: feat: post fraud ban candidates to a private Discord channel
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
The hourly fraud check only logged aggregate counts, so nobody could see who it would ban without enabling bans. This turns it into a review queue.

- Scheduled runs now always execute read-only. Bans are still written only when `FRAUD_BAN_ENABLED` is set.
- `runFraudBanCheck` returns a `report` of candidates that are not already banned, plus scanned/unmapped counts.
- When `DISCORD_FRAUD_WEBHOOK_URL` is set, the script posts a summary line with the report attached as TSV to the private `polli-admin` channel. Nothing is posted when no account needs action, so a message means someone crossed the threshold. No mentions.
- Manually banning an account removes it from the next report; no state is kept.
- Public Actions logs stay counts-only. Without the secret, nothing is posted.

gist.headline: The hive gets a watchlist
gist.blurb: Fraud checks now leave a quiet, reviewable trail for the gardeners. Candidates can be inspected in a private Discord queue before any ban switch is flipped.
gist.summary: The hourly fraud check now runs read-only by default and, when DISCORD_FRAUD_WEBHOOK_URL is configured, posts a TSV report of currently actionable, not-yet-banned candidates plus scanned and unmapped counts to the private polli-admin channel.
gist.impact: Admins get a private no-mentions review queue only when an account crosses the threshold, while public Actions logs remain counts-only and bans still require FRAUD_BAN_ENABLED.

A small monitor robot can point excitedly at a threshold marker while code-plants and flowers make the otherwise internal moderation workflow feel calm and deliberate; the scene should imply review before action, not punishment.
